safety.note: A naive string substitution into the source before parsing would emit a live <script>. Segmentation runs in the sanitizer, so the value lands in a leaf that has no children and no props.
The value tries to escape its text node by closing the enclosing element. It cannot: the tree is already built.
Each half is innocent and the join is not. Concatenation happens over resolved segment text, never over source markup.
A re-scanning implementation would resolve the inner site. There is no path from a binding value back into the tokenizer.
Escape processing is a property of the source text, not of resolved values.
Entity decoding happens in the tokenizer, before segmentation. A value that looks like an entity stays text.

attributes.note: Attribute values are never segmented. The delimiter stays literal and the binding never reaches the URI sink.
Neither half is substituted, so the sink never sees an assembled value it cannot judge.
The URI sink rejects the whole value on its own merits, exactly as it does today.
CSS injection through a value slot is not available, because the slot does not exist.
Text nodes are the only interpolation position, and they still work under the same parse.
The wholesale surface for a computed value is data-bind through the node's bindTo prop: one expression, one complete value, one sink call.

conditions.note: The legacy visibility map is keyed by expression text and collides here. The conditions array is keyed by tree position.
This is the five-way-drift case: the Rust regex ladder and the ratatui comparison helper both returned false here.

bind.note: Parentheses are not an AST node; the classification follows the expression, not its spelling.
